arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Clement argued the 1995 amendment is constitutional. He stated it protects data collected for federal highway funds. He claimed this prevents use in state and federal court litigation.
Mr. Mungia argued the statute fails the South Dakota v. Dole requirements. He stated section 409 is not conditional. He asserted the plain language shows it lacks conditional nature.

Mr. Hamilton corrected a misstatement by the opposing side's counsel. He addressed the outcome if the Court adopts the United States position. He clarified the plaintiffs' claim regarding document access.
